candidates.concept: Theatre history, dramatic texts and dramaturgy
candidates.assessment: A whole24-course feasible trial combines all six literary courses, stylistic and rhetorical analysis, creative performance, film/adaptation, cultural history and research. Greek tragedy, drama as genre, myth/performance, cinematic acting/spectatorship and feminist interpretation are real substance. Together these do not sustain theatre-history progression, dramaturgical interpretation and live production analysis. Generalliterary or cinematic research is not automatically theatre-specific inquiry.

candidates.concept: Live performance, meaning and contemporary performance culture
candidates.assessment: A second full feasible24-course trial tests creative poetic performance, independent artistic practice, all six media courses, literary/adaptation methods, climatecommunication, rhetoricteaching and culturalhistory. Voice/embodiment, mise-en-scene, mediated spectatorship, documentaryproduction andenvironmentalaesthetics are genuine bridges. They form a creative/media programme without a sustained live-theatre analytical, dramaturgical andhistorical object. Absence of actortraining or a professional licence is not the criterion.

A third full feasible24-course trial tests culturalinstitutions/history, sociology/criticaltheory, qualitativeinterviews/archives, representation/race, publicrhetoric and actualschoolteaching. Museums, publicheritageprojects, materialcultureeducation andcommunity rhetoricaleducation provide concrete responses to society/education interests. Their combined object remains cultural/social inquiry rather than theatreinstitutions, theatreeducation andperformance research. This is not a claim that UCR lacks education, archives, spectatorship or performance altogether.
